title: Principal of PUD Consultants and Professor of Urban Planning, Ain Shams University
bio: Prof. Dr. Amr Attia is Principal of PUD Consultants and Professor of Urban Planning at the Faculty of Engineering, Ain Shams University, Cairo.

He studied architecture and urban design at Ain Shams University (1991) and holds a master's degree (1994) and a PhD (1999) from University College London; his doctoral research concerned tourism planning on Egypt's North West Coast.
He has worked at PUD since 1991, was a principal director at AECOM (2011 to 2020) and vice president at WATG (2020 to 2023), and was selected as an Eisenhower Fellow in 2007.

roles.text: Ain Shams University: demonstrator (1991), teaching assistant (1994), assistant professor (1999), associate professor (2005) and Professor of Urban Planning (since 24 November 2016).

Managing Director of the Consultancy Unit for Planning and Urban Design (CUPUD), Ain Shams University, and authorised representative of the university in the National Programme for the Development of Rural Strategic Plans (supported by UN-Habitat, over 400 Egyptian villages).

Member of the Technical Committee of the Grand Egyptian Museum, coordinator of the technical committee for planning and landscaping of the area around the museum, and involved in organising and managing its UNESCO-sponsored, UIA-patronised international architecture competition.
Visiting Professor, Arab Academy for Science, Technology and Maritime Transport.

AECOM Arabia, Saudi Arabia: senior project manager, rising to Principal Director, Design, Planning and Economics. Projects included the Jeddah Stormwater Drainage Programme and the Jeddah Spatial Framework Plan.

contributions.text: Member of the SHARE Egypt 2026 organising board and its Board Chairman. The forum brings SHARE Architects to Africa for the first time.

Guided the local Egyptology and heritage experts on WATG's tourism master plan framework for the Giza Pyramids, commissioned by the Egyptian government in 2024. WATG led the plan and PUD is the cultural-heritage specialist. The framework was presented to the Ministry of Tourism in December 2025.
Jabal Thabeer Park, Makkah: concept master plan by PUD Consultants with Gillespies, Systematica and Studio 4215, for Kidana.

According to PUD, the practice led the international Steering Committee advising ACUD on the strategic master plan for Phases 2 to 4 of Egypt's New Administrative Capital, with Dar Al-Handasah as lead designer.

The Eisenhower Fellowships 2026 profile of Prof. Dr. Amr Attia records planning frameworks for Jeddah, Egypt's New Administrative Capital, AlUla and the holy sites of Makkah. It says the AlUla framework and guidelines now work as binding planning instruments within a development programme above $15 billion.

Co-author of the book chapter "Partnerships for Sustainable Tourism Development in the Cultural Heritage Sites" (with Reham Kamel El-Khadrawy and Rowaida Rashed) in Conservation of Architectural Heritage, Springer.
Author of the WATG insight article "Rejuvenation or decline? A challenge for real estate developers in the Middle East" (1 June 2021).
Author of "Utilizing Information Technologies in Urban Renewal Initiatives: Opportunities and Constraints", Humanities and Social Sciences Journal 4(1), 5 to 15.

Seminar organiser and member of the organising and scientific committees of "Linear Parks and Urban Ambiances" in Cairo, part of the Imhotep programme between Ain Shams University and the Grenoble School of Architecture (Cresson laboratory).
Co-author of "Spatial Planning and the Need for Spatial Planning Support Systems: Urbanism as Example", Journal of Al-Azhar University Engineering Sector 9(32).
Co-author of "Strategic City Planning in Egypt", Journal of Al-Azhar University Engineering Sector 7(24).

Principal in charge of the Regional Vision and Tourism Development Plan for Egypt's North West Coast (1,680 km2), with WEP (Germany) and think-GDC (Seattle) for the Tourism Development Authority and GOPP.

Co-founder of K2C (Kansas to Cairo), an online architecture studio in the Second Life virtual world linking Ain Shams University and the University of Southern California School of Architecture, with U.S. State Department funding. Architectural Record covered it in June 2010.
Author of "The Development of Urban Settlements and the New Approaches for Measuring Quality of Life Indicators", Journal of Al-Azhar University Engineering Sector (in Arabic), with A. Mostafa.
Co-editor of "The Grand Museum of Egypt: International Architecture Competition", Volumes I and II, published by the Egyptian Ministry of Culture.

Co-author (with Mohamed Salheen) of "Urban Transitional Zones in Greater Cairo Region: Problems and Opportunities", 39th ISoCaRP International Congress, Cairo, 19 to 22 October 2003. In April 2003 he also co-authored three papers (in Arabic) for the Al-Azhar Engineering Seventh International Conference.
Technical coordinator between Ain Shams University and the General Organization for Physical Planning (GOPP) for guiding plans for 53 Egyptian villages (April 2002 to April 2004).
PhD thesis on implementing tourism policy on Egypt's North West Coast, evaluating pilot tourism projects including Marina El Alamein (UCL Discovery, open access).
MSc thesis "Planning for Sustainable Tourism Development: The Case of Marina Al-Alamein Project in the North West Coast Region of Egypt" (unpublished, University of London).
Part of the team that won first prize in the international competition to design the Arab World Participation Galleries at the 56th Frankfurt Book Fair.
